title: Rodent Brain Slice Preparation for Electrophysiological Studies
author: Verónica lejandra Cáceres-Chávez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bggujtww
materials: Prepare and check all materials and equipment: Before beginning the anesthesia and dissection protocol, verify that all the necessary materials are available and in good condition (Fig. 1). The perfusion and Krebs solutions should have been prepared previously and must not be more than 7 days old. Even if the solutions are less than 7 days old but visible particulates can be seen or the solutions appear cloudy, they should not be used and new solutions should be prepared before anesthetizing the animal. The anesthesia (ketamine and xylazine mix) should also be checked by verifying that it has not passed the expiration date and there is no coloration of the liquid which could indicate oxidation. Also verify that all the dissection instruments are clean, undamaged, and laid out for easy access (Fig. 1B). Also confirm the Vibratome is in working condition. Position the large glass petri dish with glued attachment block in the Vibratome, and break a new razor blade in half and fix it in place (Fig. 1F,G). Place the other half of the blade together with a folder piece of filter paper on top of a small glass petri dish on ice (Fig. 1E). This will later be used to cut the brain before placing it in the Vibratome for slicing. Place fine tip paint brushes and forceps at the side of the Vibratome to be used when transferring brain slices from the dish to incubation chamber. Put other items, such as the cyanoacrylate glue and syringe with perfusion solution, on ice (Fig. 1C,D). It is important that all these materials are set up before anesthetizing the animal so that the dissection and brain removal can occur as quickly and smoothly as possible. Figure 1 : Dissection area and setup.

Cool and oxygenate solutions: Pour around 80 mL of perfusion (sucrose) solution into a glass beaker and cover the top of the beaker with parafilm (Fig. 2D). Place the beaker in the freezer for approximately 10-15 minutes, until the solution is partially but not completely frozen (consistency similar to a slushie). Pour around 60 mL of Krebs solution into the incubation chamber (Fig. 2E), and place the end of the tube running from the gas tank into the solution and turn the gas on to oxygenate. You should see small bubbles continuously produced in the solution (not shown) Figure 2 : Solutions used for perfusion and slicing of the brain. .

steps.title: Anesthetize the animal
steps.instruction: Administer a mixture of ketamine (85 mg/kg) and xylazine (15 mg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection.

substeps.instruction: Hold the animal by the tail and place on a flat surface; optionally cover eyes and mouth with a small cloth.
Immobilize the animal by grabbing the skin on the back of the neck just below the ears.
Turn the animal ventral side up and inject the anesthesia into the peritoneal cavity (between the abdominal midline and the leg) at a 30° angle.
Initial dose: 4-6 units for mice or 40-60 units for large rats.
Apply additional doses of 1-2 units (mice) or 10-20 units (rats) every 5-10 minutes as necessary, depending on animal weight.
Place the animal back in the cage for 5-10 minutes for the anesthesia to take effect.
Monitor motor behavior, respiratory rhythm, and responses to noxious stimuli (e.g., foot or tail pinch with atraumatic forceps).
Verify deep anesthesia (cessation of motor behavior, slow/regular respiratory rhythm, and no reflex responses) before proceeding.

steps.title: Position and restrain the animal
steps.instruction: Secure the deeply anesthetized animal in the dissecting tray.

substeps.instruction: Position the animal ventral side up in the dissecting tray.
Fix each limb to the tray using masking tape.

steps.title: Expose the thoracic wall
steps.instruction: Reveal the thoracic wall tissue using hemostatic forceps and scissors.

substeps.instruction: Use hemostatic forceps to clamp and pull up the fur and skin in the center of the thorax, using the xiphoid process as a reference point.
Cut away the fur and skin to reveal the thoracic wall tissue.

steps.title: Open the thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Open the thoracic cavity to expose the heart.

substeps.instruction: Clamp the xiphoid process with hemostatic forceps.
Using 4.5 inch scissors, cut on either side of the thoracic cavity.
Continue cutting anteriorly on both sides to fully open the cavity until the heart is visible.
Make a small incision in the right atrium using the scissors.

steps.title: Perform cardiac perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the animal with perfusion solution via the left ventricle.

substeps.instruction: Fill a 20 mL syringe (or 5 mL for mouse) with perfusion solution.
Carefully insert the needle into the left ventricle, ensuring the needle does not puncture through to the other side.
Slowly inject the solution in a pulsatile manner, synchronized with the cardiac rhythm.
Confirm successful perfusion by checking that the eyes have turned whitish.

steps.title: Sacrifice and expose the cranium
steps.instruction: Decapitate the animal and clear the skull for brain access.

substeps.instruction: Use 5.5 inch scissors to cut at the base of the cranium above the first cervical vertebra to decapitate the animal.
Use 5.5 inch scissors to carefully cut away the fur and skin to expose the cranium.

steps.title: Expose and remove the brain
steps.instruction: Carefully open the skull and extract the brain.

substeps.instruction: Using 4.5 inch scissors, cut from the occipital to temporal area on the left side, then repeat on the right side.
Perform a horizontal cut at the most anterior part of the cranium.
Cut down the midline from posterior to anterior, lifting the scissors slightly to avoid brain damage.
Gently peel away the cranial bones.
Using a small spoon, gently scoop the brain out of the cranium and place it onto filter paper in a small glass petri dish on ice.

steps.title: Prepare brain for slicing
steps.instruction: Section the brain into hemispheres and remove non-target structures.

substeps.instruction: Use a sharp razor blade to cut away the cerebellum and brainstem.
Cut the brain down the midline to separate the two hemispheres.

steps.title: Mount brain hemispheres for slicing
steps.instruction: Glue the brain hemispheres into the Vibratome petri dish.

substeps.instruction: Place two drops of cyanoacrylate glue in the glass petri dish (one on the left, one on the right, with one slightly anterior to the other).
Place a brain hemisphere on a glue drop with the cut side (midline) down and the anterior-posterior axis perpendicular to the blade for sagittal slicing.
Repeat for the second hemisphere.
Remove any extra glue using a small piece of filter paper.

steps.title: Obtain brain slices using Vibratome
steps.instruction: Cut sagittal slices of the brain using a Vibratome.

substeps.instruction: Fill the petri dish with chilled Krebs solution.
Insert the gas tank tube into the dish to oxygenate the brain.
Set the Vibratome to cut slices 200-300 microns thick at the lowest velocity and power.
After each slice, move the blade up 50 microns, return it to the original position, move it back down 50 microns, and then down an additional 200-300 microns to cut the next slice.
Repeat until most tissue is sliced (typically yielding 6-7 quality sagittal slices per hemisphere).

steps.title: Transfer and visualize slices
steps.instruction: Move slices to the appropriate chamber for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Use a fine-tip paint brush to transfer slices to an incubating chamber (for electrophysiology) or a small petri dish (for anatomy).
For neuroanatomy, place the petri dish under a light microscope.
Visualize structures (e.g., hippocampus, striatum) using various magnifications and contrasts.

steps.title: Clean up and waste disposal
steps.instruction: Sanitize the workspace and dispose of biological materials.

substeps.instruction: Place all sharps in the red sharps disposal container.
Wrap biological waste in newspaper and place it in the yellow biological waste bag.
Wipe down the work area with ethanol.
